name: Lady Jane
description: Lady Jane is a complex two-deck solitaire game belonging to the Spider family. It is characterized by its large tableau of 10 piles and the requirement to build up eight foundations in suit. On the tableau, build down alternating colors; only same-suit sequences can be moved as a unit, requiring tactical planning to keep suits together. Stock deals 3 cards at a time to waste; one redeal allowed.

content.text: Lady Jane is a complex two-deck solitaire game belonging to the Spider family. It is characterized by its large tableau of 10 piles and the requirement to build up eight foundations in suit. On the tableau, build down alternating colors; only same-suit sequences can be moved as a unit, requiring tactical planning to keep suits together. Stock deals 3 cards at a time to waste; one redeal allowed.
Part of the late 20th-century expansion of computer-based solitaire games. It evolved as a hybrid between the foundation-building of Klondike and the large-move mechanics of Spider.
One player only. Lady Jane is a solitaire (patience) game; the player manages the entire layout—ten tableau piles, eight foundations, stock, and waste—making all moves alone.
Table space for 10 tableau piles, 8 foundation piles, stock and waste.
Deal 10 tableau piles: first pile 1 card, second 2, third 3, and so on up to 10 (55 cards total). Place the remaining 49 cards face down as stock. Eight foundation piles and waste start empty.
